dismissals.because: src/forge/templates/conventions/frontend.md:61 Done-when 3 asks that production never shows the toolbar; the run-time check never loads its chunk outside APP_ENV=demo, and one Dockerfile builds one image for both, so a separate production build adds a moving part the item doesn't need

findings.body: The example sets `window.__APP_ENV__` with an inline script, but the unchanged security convention at `src/forge/templates/conventions/security.md:9` requires `app.use(helmet())`. [Helmet’s default policy](https://helmet.js.org/) uses `script-src 'self'`, which blocks that inline script. Following both conventions leaves the property unset, so the demo-only condition at line 69 never renders Agentation. Use a CSP-compatible way to provide the environment value.
findings.title: Not done: Anyone can point at the screen

findings.body: The loader counts tables before opening the insertion transaction at line 38. During an overlapping deployment, which `src/forge/templates/conventions/deploy.md:5-6` permits, the previous instance can insert a row after these counts. The loader would then add demo records to a database that is no longer empty. Coordinate the check and insertion with concurrent writers.
findings.title: Make the empty-table check atomic with demo insertion

findings.body: The stack convention calls for a first-version loader, but the unchanged prototype instructions at `src/forge/templates/skill.md:118-127` still do not tell the agent to build it or use `Words they use` for screen labels. The skill is outside TEMPLATES’ scope; SPEC must supply this instruction.
findings.title: Later: SPEC must put first-version demo data and customer labels in the skill
